angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,589,675 km at 24.68 pc = 0.86 mas. The record's radius is the volume-equivalent sphere of the fit's two radii; the fit gives the radii, not one diameter.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 59774: distance 24.685 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.004), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 24.685 +/- 0.099 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 40.3279 +/- 0.1945 mas (same row, RUWE 2.64), 207.3 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 2.285 solar radii from Jones et al. (2015), ApJ 813, 58, the table of model results under the gravity-darkening law of Espinosa Lara & Rieutord (2011), Megrez: equatorial radius 2.511 (+0.074, -0.068) and polar radius 1.893 (+0.046, -0.045) solar radii, from the Roche model fitted to CHARA visibilities and broadband photometry; the record holds the volume-equivalent sphere of the two, 2.285 solar radii, and the scene draws the flattening (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/813/1/58): 1,589,675 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 8694 +/- 1380 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 59774: effective temperature 8694 +/- 1380 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.047) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 59774: effective temperature 8694 +/- 1380 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.047) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
surfaceGravitySource: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 3.94 from 2024A&A...681A.107R; the 3 published values span log g 3.6 to 3.9433, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...681A.107R)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * del UMa: spectral type A2Vn (2003AJ....126.2048G)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * del UMa: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
luminositySource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 1575287046603605888, flags_flame 00: lum_flame 23.094496 solar luminosities (16th to 84th percentiles 22.820026 to 23.401695); its log10 is recorded
ageSource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 1575287046603605888, flags_flame 00: age_flame 0.7246109 Gyr (16th to 84th percentiles 0.6024808 to 0.846041)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * del UMa: projected rotation speed 233 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2007A&A...463..671R)

shape.qualification: A Roche surface flattened by rotation, 2.511 solar radii at the equator and 1.893 at the poles, its pole 50 degrees from the line of sight at position angle 50.9 degrees, and gravity darkened with exponent 0.17 from a 9,550 K pole: Jones et al. (2015), ApJ 813, 58 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/813/1/58). The disc color is the star's measured one; only the pole-to-equator contrast is the model's.
